Plums___Black_Knot.plant_name: Plums (Plums, prunes, tart cherries, sweet cher)

disease_symptoms.s1: Elongated, rough, velvety olive-green swellings on twigs and branches that expand over 1-2 years into hard, coal-black, cracked, brittle, knotty galls that encircle and girdle branches.
disease_symptoms.s2: Stunted vegetative growth and reduced photosynthetic vigor.
disease_symptoms.s3: Premature leaf chlorosis, yellowing, and leaf drop.
disease_symptoms.s4: Blemishes, corky scars, or rots on harvested plant organs and fruit.

disease_causes.c1: Ascospores mature in pseudothecia on 2-year-old knots during spring rainy periods and infect succulent green shoots
disease_causes.c2: The fungus stimulates abnormal cell division in xylem and bark parenchymatous tissue.
disease_causes.c3: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.
disease_causes.c4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

disease_prevention.p1: Prune out galls during dormant season, cutting at least 10-15 cm below the visible knot margin
disease_prevention.p2: Destroy or burn prunings immediately
disease_prevention.p3: Eradicate wild cherry and plum trees near commercial orchards.
disease_prevention.p4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

fertilizer_recommendation.f3: Supplement with soluble Calcium (Calcium Nitrate) and Silicon to thicken leaf epidermal barriers.

disease_symptoms.s1: Sunken or swollen reddish-orange to yellowish-brown cankers on stems and branches
disease_symptoms.s2: yellow-orange pinhead-sized fruiting pycnidia erupt through bark fissures

Potato___Late_Blight_of_Potato_and_Tomat.disease_name: Late Blight of Potato and Tomato

disease_symptoms.s1: Water-soaked, pale-to-dark green irregular spots on leaves and stems, turning dark purplish-brown with pale green margins
disease_symptoms.s2: In cool, wet weather, a delicate white fuzzy mildew appears on the lower leaf surface
disease_symptoms.s3: Infected tubers develop irregular reddish-brown granular dry rot.
disease_symptoms.s4: Blemishes, corky scars, or rots on harvested plant organs and fruit.

disease_causes.c1: Historic cause of the 1845 Irish Potato Famine
disease_causes.c2: Overwinters as mycelium in infected seed tubers, volunteer potatoes, or cull piles
disease_causes.c3: Biflagellate zoospores emerge from sporangia in free water and infect plants rapidly within hours.
disease_causes.c4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

disease_prevention.p1: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers
disease_prevention.p2: Eliminate cull piles and volunteer potatoes
disease_prevention.p3: Ensure wide plant spacing
disease_prevention.p4: Destroy haulms (vines) 2 weeks before harvest.

Snow Mold.scientific_name: Typhula incarnata / Typhula ishikariensis (Gray Snow Mold) / Microdochium nivale (Pink Snow Mold)

disease_symptoms.s1: Bleached, matted, straw-colored circular patches (20-60 cm) appearing upon winter snowmelt
disease_symptoms.s2: gray snow mold shows tiny reddish-brown to black seed-like sclerotia embedded in leaves
disease_symptoms.s3: pink snow mold develops a faint salmon-pink fuzzy mycelium when exposed to daylight.
disease_symptoms.s4: Blemishes, corky scars, or rots on harvested plant organs and fruit.

disease_causes.c4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

disease_causes.c2: CMV and Potyviruses are stylet-borne non-persistently by aphids (Aphis gossypii, Myzus persicae).
disease_causes.c3: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.
disease_causes.c4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

disease_prevention.p4: Use certified virus-free seed.

disease_symptoms.s1: Vein clearing followed by an unmistakable network of brilliant yellow veins enclosing islands of green tissue
disease_symptoms.s2: complete chlorosis in advanced stages
disease_symptoms.s3: fruits become dwarfed, malformed, tough, and yellowish-green
disease_symptoms.s4: up to 80-100% crop loss if infected early.

disease_causes.c1: Transmitted by the whitefly (Bemisia tabaci)
disease_causes.c2: Population peaks during hot summer months
disease_causes.c3: Virus overwinters on roadside weeds like Croton sparsiflorus and Ageratum.
disease_causes.c4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

disease_prevention.p1: Destroy weed hosts around okra plots
disease_prevention.p2: Grow resistant varieties like 'Arka Anamika', 'Arka Abhay', 'Punjab Padmini', 'Parbhani Kranti'
disease_prevention.p3: Rogue out infected plants within 20 days.
disease_prevention.p4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

disease_symptoms.s1: Crisp, slender green pods with uniform color and smooth epidermal surface.

disease_causes.c1: Well-aerated loamy soil with active Rhizobium nitrogen-fixing root nodules and balanced moisture.

disease_prevention.p1: Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-legume crops to keep soil-borne pathogens in check.
disease_prevention.p2: Water at soil level early in the morning to prevent damp leaves and fungal spore germination.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical intervention required for healthy legumes.

disease_control.ctrl1: Provide sturdy trellising for pole varieties to ensure maximum air circulation.

disease_symptoms.s1: Glossy, firm deep-purple fruits with fresh bright green calyx and unblemished skin.

organic_remedies.org1: Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) foliar spray every 10 days as a natural repellent.

disease_control.ctrl1: Stake heavy fruiting branches to keep purple eggplants off damp soil surfaces.

Downy_mildew.severity: Moderate to High (Rapid Spoilage in Cool, Humid Conditions)

disease_symptoms.s1: Angular, pale green to bright chlorotic yellow patches on the upper leaf surface delineated by leaf veins.
disease_symptoms.s2: Purplish-gray to brown downy felt or fungal sporulation on the corresponding underside of the leaves in humid weather.
disease_symptoms.s3: Severe infections cause rapid foliar browning, leaf curl, and premature defoliation.

disease_causes.c1: Water mold oospores and sporangia driven by extended leaf wetness (>6 hours) and high humidity (>85%).
disease_causes.c2: Temperatures between 15°C and 22°C (59°F–72°F) coupled with dense, unventilated plant spacing.

disease_prevention.p1: Provide wide plant spacing and north-south row alignment to accelerate leaf drying from morning sunlight.
disease_prevention.p2: Use drip or furrow irrigation exclusively; never apply overhead sprinklers during evening or overcast periods.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Balanced N-P-K nutrition (10-10-10 or 8-16-16) with supplemental potassium silicate to fortify epidermal leaf cell walls.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Avoid heavy spring nitrogen applications which promote excessively soft, vulnerable succulence.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: Curative systemic fungicides: Mefenoxam + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold MZ), Cymoxanil (Curzate), or Dimethomorph (Acrobat 50WP).
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Protectant contact fungicides: Copper hydroxide (Kocide 3000) or Chlorothalonil applied every 7-10 days.

organic_remedies.org1: Bio-fungicides containing Bacillus subtilis (Serenade ASO) or Trichoderma harzianum as early preventive sprays.
organic_remedies.org2: Potassium bicarbonate (MilStop) or copper octanoate (copper soap) to suppress spore germination without synthetic residue.

disease_control.ctrl1: Scout lower canopy leaves twice weekly and immediately rogue out early infected leaves into sealed bags.
disease_control.ctrl2: Rotate out of host crop families for a minimum of 2-3 years after harvest.

disease_symptoms.s3: Compact rosette growth habit with vigorous crown and white fibrous roots.

disease_causes.c1: Cool-season growth under moist, organic-rich soil (pH 6.5–7.0) with consistent moisture.

disease_prevention.p1: Maintain consistent shallow cultivation to suppress weeds without disturbing spinach's delicate feeder roots.
disease_prevention.p2: Ensure afternoon shade or shade cloth during warm spells to prevent premature bolting.

fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Light side-dressing of balanced organic 5-5-5 fertilizer during peak rosette leaf expansion.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical intervention needed for healthy spinach.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Insecticidal soap or neem spray if leaf miner scouts or aphids are detected on outer leaves.

organic_remedies.org1: Apply a thin layer of compost mulch around crowns to regulate soil temperature and prevent soil splashing.
organic_remedies.org2: Companion planting with radishes, onions, and strawberries to naturally deter pests.

disease_control.ctrl1: Harvest outer leaves continuously (cut-and-come-again) to promote vigorous center leaf development.

disease_symptoms.s1: Firm, rounded globe-shaped crimson-purple taproot with smooth skin and unbroken crown.
disease_symptoms.s2: Vibrant upright green and maroon foliage free from Cercospora leaf spot or downy mildew.
disease_symptoms.s3: Crisp internal rings with deep ruby coloration and sweet, earthy flavor.

disease_causes.c1: Loose, stone-free sandy loam soil with adequate boron and neutral pH (6.0–6.8).

disease_prevention.p1: Thin beet seedlings early to 7-10 cm apart to ensure unobstructed root bulb expansion.
disease_prevention.p2: Maintain uniform soil moisture to prevent woody texture, root splitting, or internal ring discoloration.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: High-potassium and phosphorus fertilizer (NPK 5-10-10 or bone meal with wood ash) to promote bulb sizing.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Apply trace micronutrient boron (Solubor at 1.5 g/L) if soil is boron-deficient to prevent internal black heart.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical fungicide or pesticide required for prime healthy beetroot.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Diatomaceous earth dusting around seedlings to stop flea beetles.

organic_remedies.org1: Mulch beds with aged straw or shredded leaves to maintain cool root temperatures.
organic_remedies.org2: Incorporate well-rotted leaf mold compost before sowing to loosen heavy clay soil.

disease_control.ctrl1: Harvest roots when they reach 5–8 cm in diameter for prime tenderness and maximum nutritional value.

disease_symptoms.s1: Plump, crisp, and firm scarlet or white taproots with smooth surface and zero splitting.
disease_symptoms.s2: Healthy green lyrate lobed leaves with vibrant coloration and no flea beetle shot-hole damage.
disease_symptoms.s3: Crisp, peppery white internal flesh without pithiness or internal discoloration.

disease_causes.c1: Fast-growing cool-season conditions (21-30 days to maturity) in light, friable, moisture-retentive soil.

disease_prevention.p1: Sow successionally every 10–14 days for a continuous crisp harvest throughout spring and autumn.
disease_prevention.p2: Cover fresh beds with lightweight floating row covers immediately after seeding to exclude root maggots.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Low-nitrogen organic compost; excess nitrogen creates oversized leafy tops with diminutive, split roots.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Light application of aged wood ash or potassium sulfate to enhance root firmness.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No synthetic chemical intervention required for fast-turnaround healthy radishes.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Spinosad or pyrethrin spot-spray only if intense flea beetle infestation occurs.

organic_remedies.org1: Dust bed perimeter with wood ash or neem cake powder to deter subterranean larvae.
organic_remedies.org2: Keep soil evenly damp; drought stress triggers harsh bitterness, premature bolting, and woody pith.

disease_control.ctrl1: Harvest promptly when roots reach golf-ball diameter; leaving radishes in soil causes rapid pithiness.

disease_symptoms.s1: Firm, plump, aromatic rhizome fingers with thin, tan skin and yellow fibrous flesh.
disease_symptoms.s2: Erect, reed-like pseudostems with vibrant lanceolate green leaves free from leaf spot or bacterial wilt.
disease_symptoms.s3: Clean root buds showing vigorous sprouts with no softness, foul smell, or water-soaking.

disease_causes.c1: Rich, well-draining warm soil with high organic matter, partial canopy shade, and high humidity.

disease_prevention.p1: Plant only certified disease-free, plump seed rhizomes treated with Trichoderma viride.
disease_prevention.p2: Ensure raised beds with excellent internal drainage to prevent rhizome rot (soft rot).

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: High-potassium organic fertilizer (NPK 8-8-16) applied in 3 split doses during active tillering.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Top-dress with well-rotted farmyard manure (FYM) or neem cake at 45 and 90 days after planting.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical intervention needed for healthy rhizomes.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Preventive drench with Mancozeb (0.2%) or Copper Oxychloride (0.25%) before monsoon.

organic_remedies.org1: Mulch generously with green leaves (10-12 tons/ha) at planting and repeated after 45 days to conserve moisture and suppress weeds.
organic_remedies.org2: Soil solarization of seedbeds prior to planting to eradicate soil-borne Pythium and Ralstonia.

disease_control.ctrl1: Hill up soil around ginger pseudostems periodically to protect expanding rhizome hands from sun-greening.
